definition: XML retrieval, or XML information retrieval, is the content-based retrieval of documents structured with XML (eXtensible Markup Language).
details: As such it is used for computing relevance of XML documents.

explainer.lead: XML retrieval finds content inside documents whose structure is marked up in XML. It matters because structure lets a system target a specific field or section rather than the whole document.

tiers.eli5: It is like searching a filing cabinet where every folder, tab and sheet is labelled, so you can ask for one labelled part instead of reading everything.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers score queries against individual XML elements, combining content match with structural constraints. A common pitfall is ignoring structure so results return whole documents instead of the precise element the user asked for.
tiers.paperLevel: Relevance is computed over XML elements rather than whole documents, typically combining content similarity with structural constraints; precision at element level is hard because small elements can match many queries loosely.

explainer.example: A query asks for a title element containing a given phrase, and the system returns the matching title elements with their relevance scores rather than the full documents.
